movie.title: How to Divorce During the War
movie.overview: Vilnius 2022. High-flying executive Marija chooses the worst possible moment for an honest conversation with her husband Vytas about divorcing - just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine goes into full scale. Now they must navigate the process of separation as it collides with a refugee and mid-life crisis.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Just as Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, a Vilnius executive's attempt to divorce her husband devolves into a tumultuous blend of mid-life angst, personal grief, and geopolitical catastrophe.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: In early 2022, corporate executive Marija decides to finally end her marriage to Vytas in Vilnius. Her timing couldn't be worse, as her declaration coincides directly with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. As panic spreads across Eastern Europe, the couple must navigate the legal and emotional chaos of their separation alongside a burgeoning refugee crisis. The looming war amplifies their existential mid-life crossroad, forcing them to re-evaluate what truly matters amid absolute uncertainty.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Set against the tense backdrop of Vilnius in late February 2022, high-flying executive Marija initiates a crucial, long-overdue conversation with her husband, Vytas, requesting a divorce. However, their personal implosion is instantly overshadowed when Russia launches its full-scale military invasion of neighboring Ukraine the very next morning. As shockwaves ripple through Lithuania, society shifts into emergency mode with citizens rallying to support incoming refugees and prepare for potential regional escalation. Caught in this extraordinary atmosphere, Marija and Vytas struggle to carry out the bureaucratic and psychological logistics of uncoupling. Petty marital grievances and mid-life anxieties clash sharply with the existential horror unfolding across the border, exposing the stark absurdity of individual domestic drama in a time of global peril. Through encounters with displaced families, anxious friends, and shifting priorities, both partners are forced to confront their internal voids. Ultimately, as the chaos outside mirrors their internal collapse, Marija and Vytas are compelled to redefine their duty to each other and themselves in an abruptly transformed world.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set in Vilnius in February 2022, 'How to Divorce During the War' follows Marija, an accomplished corporate executive who reaches a breaking point in her marriage and demands a divorce from her husband, Vytas. Her announcement coincides with Russia's sudden full-scale invasion of Ukraine, plunging Europe into crisis and turning their quiet lives upside down overnight. As panic, humanitarian efforts, and refugee influxes reshape the city's social fabric, Marija and Vytas find their personal separation inextricably entangled with the surrounding historical catastrophe. Blending personal drama with mid-life angst and geopolitical reality, the narrative offers a poignant, spoiler-free exploration of modern relationships, emotional resilience, and human absurdity when intimate domestic crises collide with historic tragedy.

story_structure.climax: The pressure of external wartime realities and internal relationship grievances reaches a peak, forcing Marija and Vytas into an emotional confrontation where they must choose how to treat one another when everything around them is falling apart.
story_structure.conflict: Just as Marija initiates the divorce, Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, immediately destabilizing their personal plans and plunging their surrounding world into chaos.
story_structure.resolution: With the initial wave of crisis settling into a new reality, both individuals establish a path forward, finding closure and redefining their individual futures against the backdrop of an altered world.
story_structure.introduction: Marija, a high-flying Vilnius executive, decides to end her marriage to her husband Vytas, setting the stage for a personal life transition amidst a turbulent mid-life crisis.
story_structure.risingAction: As refugees flood into Vilnius and geopolitical tension escalates, Marija and Vytas are forced to navigate the bureaucratic and emotional logistics of separating while simultaneously responding to the humanitarian crisis around them.
